STEP 2 - Ruler: The square dish is about 20 cm across its diagonal-ish width, so I'll use roughly 19 cm. Its area is about 19 × 19 × 0.85 ≈ 300 cm² (rounded-square shape).

STEP 3 - Items: Whole almonds (about 30 pieces).

STEP 4 - Area: The almonds occupy a cluster of about 8 cm × 8 cm, roughly 50 cm² including gaps. That is about 17% of the dish.

STEP 5 - Volume: Count-based check. Each almond is about 2.2 cm × 1.2 cm × 0.8 cm, which is about 1.1 ml. For about 30 almonds, that is about 33 ml. The area method gives 50 cm² × 1.0 cm = 50 ml of gross volume. I'll use the piece-based size and take about 40 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: An almond weighs about 1.2 g each, so 30 almonds is about 36 g. Bulk density of about 0.65 g/ml × 50 ml ≈ 33 g. This agrees, so I'll use about 36 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Almonds are about 579 kcal/100 g, so 36 g ≈ 208 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 30 almonds is a small handful, roughly 35 g, which is plausible.
